title: Empirical Evaluation of a Generate–Validate–Repair Loop for Intent→Network Configuration Using a Deterministic Reachability Validator
abstract: We quantify the marginal effect of inserting a deterministic reachability validator plus at most one automated repair (a generate–validate–repair, GVR, loop) around a single LLM (declared gpt-5-mini) for mapping natural-language NetOps intents to device configurations. In a fully preregistered paired design (cns-m2026-01) using shared-initial semantics on 300 intents (600 episodes), the baseline generator produced execution-validated correct configurations in 299/300 tasks (99.667%). The guarded pipeline (deterministic validator ± one repair) produced 300/300 (100.0%). Paired difference = 0.00333; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Provider-call accounting shows 301 total model calls (300 shared-initial generator calls + 1 repair call). The preregistered target improvement (10 percentage points) is not supported because the baseline generator was near ceiling on this task set. All per-episode model-call traces, validator traces, scoring JSON, and analysis artifacts are archived with SHA‑256 hashes (Disclosure) to enable reproducible reanalysis and extension.

sections.introduction:
Motivation. Large language models promise to make intent-driven network automation practical by translating high-level operator intent into device-specific configuration. However, operational adoption requires both correctness with respect to the intent and assurance that no unintended reachability or policy regressions are introduced. One widely proposed architecture places a deterministic validator (reachability/policy checker) between a proposer (LLM) and execution and optionally adds automated repair to form a closed-loop generate–validate–repair (GVR) pipeline. This experiment measures the marginal benefit of adding a single deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair call around a single LLM generator (declared gpt-5-mini) on a controlled NetOps intent corpus.
Research question and contributions. The preregistered research question (cns-m2026-01) asks: does wrapping an LLM generator with a deterministic reachability validator and allowing at most one automated repair increase the paired rate of execution-validated, intent-satisfying configurations versus the same generator run without the gate? Contributions: (1) a fully preregistered paired experiment with shared-initial semantics (N=300 pairs) and complete artifact archiving; (2) a deterministic validator implementation and per-episode validator traces; (3) the run-level result, accounting, and analysis artifacts (counts, exact paired test, bootstrap CI), all published with SHA‑256 indexes; (4) reproducible failure accounting exposing how a single repair corrected the lone baseline error and illustrating practical boundaries of single-step GVR on a high-baseline-accuracy task set.
sections.related_work: Positioning. Recent NetOps literature explores intent→configuration, verifier-assisted pipelines, and generate–validate–repair ideas in code and configuration domains (see cited_record_ids). Prior surveys and prototypes motivate closed-loop checking and repair but often lack fully preregistered paired measurements with complete execution provenance. Our work provides an artifact-grounded confirmation test of the marginal effect of a single-step deterministic validator+repair wrapper on an LLM generator in a controlled emulator setting. We do not claim generality across models, validators, or intent distributions; instead we report an evidence-backed, reproducible quantification and the exact artifacts needed for extensions.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. The experiment was preregistered as cns-m2026-01 (preregistration SHA‑256 = 0726a6c02c1ed6fc379927f4bb0696330f0b00484f15caee5cf4ebc072316bf7). The design is paired (within-intent) with shared-initial semantics: for each intent a single generator proposal was produced and then evaluated both as baseline (no validator) and as guarded (validator ± one repair). Task selection: 300 intent→configuration tasks were deterministically drawn from the preregistered generator after contamination filtering; the task manifest is archived at execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 91564bb69ac692e2fbd6321708863d13938309b5433ef1b211541ba5426df990). The execution contract declared gpt-5-mini as the single model (see execution/model_configuration.json; SHA‑256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820).
Shared-initial semantics, generator, and guarded pipeline. For each intent a single generator call (shared-initial) produced the candidate configuration used in both conditions. Guarded processing applies a deterministic, closed-world reachability validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, version 5.0) that: (a) parses commands, (b) simulates their effect in an emulator snapshot, (c) checks the proposal satisfies the declared final-state constraints and the task’s allowed_touched_fields, and (d) detects any emulator-observed changes outside allowed fields (these are "unintended reachability changes"). If the validator rejects, the pipeline permits at most one automated repair call (preregistered repair budget = 1). Implementation identifiers and emulator snapshot references are enumerated in execution/transformation_manifest.json (SHA‑256 = b6ba6a75fa59f12f6b67e16aa5702f0fb95ba94cdb8d9b7e4d9b530c1ea76eb1).
Scoring and outcomes. Outcome per pair is binary: 1 if the generator proposal, when executed, satisfies the intent and produces no unintended reachability changes as determined by the validator/emulator; otherwise 0. Confirmatory test: exact McNemar two‑sided test on discordant pairs, preregistered. Complementary uncertainty quantification: bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the paired difference (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). The analysis executor recorded parameters and results in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 7db06f53d650b2ffc5838b392740c75681480829e5db575e44a9a065eadb965e). Note: the analysis was executed by the registered executor 'paired_binary_analysis_v1' (see analysis artifacts). The execution manifest records provider-call accounting and a full path-to-hash index for every stored artifact (execution/execution_manifest.json). No separate ad-hoc post-hoc tests were introduced; all confirmatory computations follow the preregistered plan.
Reproducibility footprint. Every model response, provider-call trace, validator trace, per-episode scoring JSON, task manifest, and analysis artifact is archived with SHA‑256; representative archived files and SHA values are cited in Results and the Disclosure. The full call cache and provider traces are under execution/provider_calls/ and execution/call_cache/ (the manifest contains the complete index). The analysis was run by the registered executor; its run parameters (bootstrap resamples, seed, and exact test choice) are in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (SHA‑256 cited above). There is no separate unarchived analysis script: the analysis executor and its recorded run log are the authoritative provenance for the statistical computations.
sections.results:
Execution and accounting. The run completed all planned episodes: planned_episode_count = 600; completed_episode_count = 600; failed_episode_count = 0. Provider-call accounting (execution manifest) records model_calls_used = 301 (300 generator shared-initial calls + 1 guarded repair call). The single repair call is logged at execution/provider_calls/task-000117-guarded-repair.json (SHA‑256 = 4deb410d5736ab332cd5caaf00b16051e5b0aef2276255c0770098f63cb523ba). The per-condition summary is archived in analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = 55eacb88c64f29dc9c5ce1ca7079eca9b4a94b5d3a2970dae019a81a1decf73b).
Primary confirmatory outcome. The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA‑256 = 3421adb52d5791a979397368165fc2062e6b9a4a771ce49c0bcac80b02215d55): n11 = 299, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Baseline successes = 299/300 = 0.996667; guarded successes = 300/300 = 1.000000. Paired difference = 0.0033333333333332993. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0 (see analysis log; the two‑sided exact test probability for the observed discordant pattern given the null yields p=1.0 when only a single one-sided discordant event is observed; see clarification below). Bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729; analysis/analysis_log.jsonl records these parameters; SHA‑256 cited above).
Why p = 1.0 with n10=1,n01=0. For small discordant counts the exact two‑sided McNemar test enumerates the tail probability of observing outcomes at least as extreme as the observed discordant counts under the null of equal discordant probabilities. With only a single discordant pair in one direction (n10=1,n01=0) the exact two‑sided tail equals 1.0 under the test’s standard construction (the observed outcome is not improbable under the null given the small sample of discordances), hence the p-value reported by the registered exact test is 1.0. The analysis log files contain the exact test invocation and parameters (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl; SHA‑256 cited above). This numeric behavior is documented in standard exact McNemar implementations and is reproducible from the archived contingency table and the registered executor.
Representative artifacts. Example per-episode scoring JSON and response files are archived (execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA‑256 = 2e4a1ef1389a18cfc5a0d6728d0978879c6675125b090b66c2dbd97b730ef153; execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 = 8f38c8becd7e1e36d8902e9ba2f09218baad021d77365b20eb52914a4bdf4080). The single observed repair episode is task-000117; its repair provider trace is execution/provider_calls/task-000117-guarded-repair.json (SHA‑256 = 4deb410d5736ab332cd5caaf00b16051e5b0aef2276255c0770098f63cb523ba). All per-episode artifacts are indexed in execution/execution_manifest.json and the task manifest (SHA‑256 values provided earlier). The analysis artifacts (paired table and summaries) are available with SHA‑256 values above.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and operational implications. The guarded pipeline corrected a single isolated baseline error (the lone discordant pair) at the cost of a single additional model call. On this controlled emulator-backed task set the baseline generator’s accuracy was near ceiling; therefore the aggregate measurable benefit from a single-step validator+one-repair wrapper was small. This run supports the practical point that a deterministic validator with a small repair budget can fix isolated generator mistakes, but an operationally meaningful reduction in residual failures will be most visible when the baseline generator performs substantially worse (noisy human-written intents, adversarial prompts), when validators check richer properties, or when repair budgets permit iterative fixes. The single observed guarded repair (task-000117) is fully archived to enable forensic inspection.
H2 and exploratory questions. H2 (that residual failures after the GVR loop are dominated by underspecified intents) was preregistered. Because there were zero residual guarded failures in this run, H2 could not be tested here; we report this limitation candidly. Exploratory metrics (repair-iteration histogram, failure-mode categorization) are recorded: the repair-iterations-to-success histogram shows 299 zero-repair successes and 1 single-repair success (figure caption and archived data). The validator–execution discrepancy rate (validator passed but emulator execution shows unintended change) was zero in this evidence set.
Robustness and sensitivity. We used an exact two‑sided McNemar test (prespecified) and a bootstrap percentile CI (10k resamples, seed=1729) to quantify uncertainty. The bootstrap CI lower bound at 0.00 reflects the ceiling baseline; the full analysis log records the exact test invocation and bootstrap parameters (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl; SHA‑256 cited above). The registered analysis executor name is paired_binary_analysis_v1; its run is the authoritative provenance for the statistical computations. No post‑hoc changes to the confirmatory test or resampling plan occurred.
sections.conclusion: A deterministic reachability validator plus a single automated repair call corrected a single isolated baseline error in this preregistered paired experiment (N=300). The guard delivered a small absolute improvement because the baseline generator was nearly perfect on the chosen deterministic emulator tasks. The evidence supports the practical value of verifier-assisted repair for isolated failures and provides a fully archived starting point for future work that evaluates harder intent distributions, iterative repair strategies, or multi-model comparisons. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived with SHA‑256 hashes for reproducible reanalysis.

disclosure_statement:
Disclosure Statement — archived provenance and runtime facts

Initial master prompt immutable reference (archived): provenance/master_prompt.txt — SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba.
Preregistration: cns-m2026-01 (preregistration SHA‑256 = 0726a6c02c1ed6fc379927f4bb0696330f0b00484f15caee5cf4ebc072316bf7). The preregistration froze the paired shared-initial design, contamination/exclusion rules, stopping and retry policy, repair budget (≤1), the confirmatory exact McNemar two‑sided test, and the bootstrap CI plan (10,000 resamples, seed=1729).
Declared LLM(s) and model identifiers: declared_model_version = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json — SHA‑256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The run used the registered hosted provider traces and the call-cache recorded under execution/provider_calls/ and execution/call_cache/ (full manifest in execution/execution_manifest.json — see artifact index for exact per-call files and SHA‑256 values).
Agentic/orchestration framework and allowed tools: a hosted generate→validator→(optional repair) orchestration was used under the adapter_family 'hosted_netops_gvr_v1'. The deterministic reachability validator component identifier is deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (version 5.0); its operational checks and emulator snapshot identifiers appear in execution/transformation_manifest.json (SHA‑256 = b6ba6a75fa59f12f6b67e16aa5702f0fb95ba94cdb8d9b7e4d9b530c1ea76eb1). No external human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the autonomy lock; all manuscript text derives from the autonomous run and archived artifacts.
Practical execution notes and archives: the full execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json) lists every stored artifact and its SHA‑256. Representative artifacts: execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 91564bb69ac692e2fbd6321708863d13938309b5433ef1b211541ba5426df990), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 3421adb52d5791a979397368165fc2062e6b9a4a771ce49c0bcac80b02215d55), analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 7db06f53d650b2ffc5838b392740c75681480829e5db575e44a9a065eadb965e), execution/provider_calls/task-000117-guarded-repair.json (SHA‑256 = 4deb410d5736ab332cd5caaf00b16051e5b0aef2276255c0770098f63cb523ba), execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 = 8f38c8becd7e1e36d8902e9ba2f09218baad021d77365b20eb52914a4bdf4080). The registered analysis executor was 'paired_binary_analysis_v1' and its run parameters (exact McNemar invocation, bootstrap resamples, seed) are recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (SHA‑256 cited above). No separate unarchived ad-hoc analysis script exists; the registered executor run and its log are the authoritative statistical provenance.
Autonomy boundary and human roles. The Research Director selected the topic family and constrained the initial master prompt pre-lock; pre-lock infrastructure development and rehearsals occurred but were not used as empirical evidence. After the autonomy lock, the AI autonomously conducted literature review, gap selection, preregistration, experiment execution, artifact archiving, analysis, and manuscript drafting. No manual technical edits to the manuscript were made after the lock. Technical retries occurred only under the preregistered retry policy; failed_episode_count = 0 and all retries (if any) are logged in execution/execution_log.jsonl.
Limitations and reproducibility statement. The run is reproducible from the provided artifact bundle: every model call, provider trace, validator trace, scoring JSON, and analysis output is archived with SHA‑256. The validator is a closed-world emulator proxy for reachability and policy checks; its semantics and snapshot identifiers are recorded in execution/transformation_manifest.json. The evidence bundle is sufficient to (a) replay the sequence of model calls and validator checks, (b) re-run the registered analysis executor on the archived contingency table and reproduce the exact McNemar p-value and bootstrap CI (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl records the exact parameters used). See Analysis and Artifacts sections for paths and SHA‑256 values.
limitations: Ceiling effect: baseline success = 299/300 reduces power to detect large preregistered improvements (target = 10 percentage points).
Task scope and external validity: deterministic emulator-backed intent corpus; results do not directly generalise to noisy, adversarial, or human-authored intent distributions in production.
Model scope: single declared model (gpt-5-mini); no cross-model generality claimed.

Validator construct validity: safety operationalised as absence of emulator-observed unintended reachability changes under a closed-world snapshot; real-world safety surfaces may be broader than this proxy.
Repair budget: only a single automated repair attempt was permitted; iterative multi-call repair strategies were not evaluated in this confirmatory run.
